title: Divide a 0.9 kg dough log into four pieces with bench scrapers, chopping at the marks
instruction: Divide the dough log into four separate pieces with the bench scrapers, cutting it at the three marks on the bench's edge, and put the scrapers down clear of the dough.
context: Home bakers divide a log of dough into equal pieces for rolls, buns and pizza bases: chop straight down with a bench scraper at marked points, and the pieces come out the same size. Anyone watching a ten-second clip sees at once what is happening and why it is hard: the edge must go straight down at the mark, not drag and smear the dough or pull the log along the bench, and not stop short and leave two pieces joined by a crease. Dough that reaches the floor is binned. The job is done when four pieces lie in line, apart, with the scrapers down and nobody holding anything.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up; arm bases at y +30.5 cm and -30.5 cm. (1) A fixed maple bench top, 240 x 400 mm (x 100 to 340 mm, y -200 to +200 mm), 12 mm thick, its top face 40 mm over the table on two 20 mm rails, so there is a 28 mm void under it. Three slots, 100 x 12 mm, cut through it at y -64, 0 and +64 mm (x 170 to 270 mm). Three black marks, 20 mm long, are printed on its back edge at the same y. (2) A loose block of bread dough (about 1.10 g/mL, floured), 256 x 80 x 40 mm, 0.90 kg, along y from y -128 to +128 mm, centred at x 220 mm, standing on the bench top; the three marks divide it into four portions of 64 mm. It is made of four pieces and three 10 mm cut strips over the slots, the pieces 59, 54, 54 and 59 mm long (207, 190, 190, 207 g); each piece is fixed to the next until the strip between them is through. A strip is the dough's full 80 x 40 mm section, 9.4 mm wide, and slides straight down its slot, 40 mm to the table. (3) Two loose bench scrapers, 0.15 kg each: a stainless blade 6 x 3 in (152.4 x 76.2 mm), 2.5 mm thick in the model, with a dark bar handle 120 x 22 x 16 mm along its back; each stands on its edge on the table in its own fixed rest (two 12 mm rails 30 mm tall, 150 mm long, with a 4 mm slot between them), the right one at x 220, y -300 mm and the left one at x 220, y +300 mm, blade along x. A strip does not give until an edge presses it with more than about 1.5 N (a design figure); from there it goes down in step with the edge at about 2.5 N for 16 mm/s, stays where it is left once 1 mm down, and springs back only within that first millimetre. Nothing else is on the table. Real trial dough (yeast-free, so it does not rise): 560 g plain flour, 330 g water and 10 g salt, kneaded 5 min, rested covered 20 min at 20 to 22 C, shaped in a 256 x 80 x 40 mm tray to 900 g, used within 30 min; a fresh batch per trial. Bench dusted with 5 g flour.
scoring: End state, read at the last step from the poses of the four pieces and two scrapers, the strips' joint positions and both grippers. A cut is made at a mark when both hold: the strip there has been pressed 37 mm or more down its slot at some time, and at some time a scraper's edge was in it: blade upright (plane within 15 degrees of vertical, length within 15 degrees of along x), its centre line within 4.7 mm plus 1 mm of the mark (the strip is 9.4 mm wide), its middle within 36 mm of the log's centre line, and the edge below the log's mid height. A strip pushed down by anything else does not count. Creased: a strip pressed more than 4 mm in and not through. Dragged (latched): any piece 12 mm or more from where it began along the bench, or turned 8 degrees or more. In line: every piece's centre within 30 mm of the log's centre line, in order along y. Tools down: both scrapers' lowest points no more than 10 mm below the table and neither within 2 mm of a piece. Hands off: on every step of the last 1 s both grippers' finger zones are 30 mm or more from all pieces and scrapers, and over that 1 s each part moves under 5 mm and turns under 5 degrees (nothing visibly moves). Score 0 if at any time a piece goes lower than 10 mm below the bench top (off the bench: binned), if no cut is made, and 0 unless hands off. Otherwise: 1.0 three cuts, no crease, not dragged, in line, tools down; 0.5 three cuts otherwise, or two cuts; 0.25 one cut. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. Doing nothing scores 0. In a real trial, per condition: a cut, the pieces fully parted with the cut faces flat (a photo from the side) and the edge shown on video inside the 9.4 mm of the mark (marks on the bench, 1 mm ruler); creased, two pieces still joined by dough; dragged, a 12 mm ruler against each piece's start line and an 8 degree angle gauge; in line, a 30 mm ruler from the centre line and the order by eye; tools down, a 2 mm feeler; hands off, a 30 mm spacer against each hand, and the video of the last 1 s showing no piece or scraper visibly move (a 5 mm mark on the bench); binned, the 10 mm drop by eye. Weigh each separate piece on a 1 g scale (log 900 g over 256 mm, 3.5 g/mm; a portion is a quarter of the pieces' combined weight, 225 g if nothing is lost). A piece still joined across n portions should weigh n portions. A cut counts only if the video shows the edge within 5.7 mm of the mark and the pieces on both sides weigh within 8 percent of their expected weight (18 g of a 225 g portion, 5.1 mm of cut position). A piece out of tolerance voids the cuts at its ends; the tier follows the cuts left (three 1.0, two 0.5, one 0.25, none 0). Pieces together under 85 percent of the weigh-in: binned, 0. The sim's pieces (207, 190, 190, 207 g) are within 8.5 g of their 198.5 g portion (4.3 percent), 794 g is 88 percent.
fidelity: Rigid bodies and sliding links. Declared: the dough is four rigid pieces and three strips (links on springs and dampers sliding down slots in the bench top, the dough squeezed out of the cut; 12 percent of the log's mass); each pair of pieces is bonded until its strip is through. Press figures are design values, not dough's (est). Blade 2.5 mm thick (real 0.9). Friction 0.35 floured dough, 0.30 steel (est). Scraper mass, handle and slots are estimates; a real bench has no slots.
reset_notes: Re-form the log in a few minutes: press fresh or leftover dough (re-kneaded, under 30 min out of the fridge) into a 256 x 80 x 40 mm tray, weigh 900 g, turn it out onto the floured bench (5 g flour). Mark the three cut points with a ruler and marker on the bench edge, at 64, 128 and 192 mm from the right end. Stand each scraper in its rest, blade along x. Wipe flour off the grippers; fit a food-safe nitrile or silicone cover on the pads.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0 (demo run under the earlier, stricter 1 mm and 0.3 degree stillness check)
